We prove that rotary encodings make the attention logit a function of relative offset alone, an exact equivariance, so whatever selection rule is learned at training lengths is reproduced verbatim at every longer length. Learned absolute encodings instead leave out-of-range positions unconstrained, and the trained head pins to a fixed absolute position inside the training range. We characterize the learned rotary rule as a low-rank ``carrier'' kernel aligned with the target offset, and we derive the resulting graceful accuracy decay as an attention-dilution law; both predictions are confirmed across seeds and offsets. A linear-attention control shows the mechanism is specific to softmax: without normalization, training selects a min-norm interpolant that does not extrapolate. The phenomenon, the equivariance, and the carrier all transfer to a multi-layer, multi-head transformer trained on a full-sequence length-generalization task. The account connects the implicit bias of attention, implicit bias for extrapolation in recurrent models, and the learning side of the RASP-L conjecture.

AI.tldr: Rotary relative encodings yield exact equivariance to relative offset, enabling length generalization beyond training; learned absolute encodings do not and instead lock to training-length positions. The optimization bias of gradient descent selects the relative-rule solution, predicting graceful decay via an attention-dilution law and a low-rank carrier kernel; this behavior extends to full transformers and connects to RASP-L conjecture.
AI.motivation: Explain the robustness of length generalization observed with relative vs absolute encodings, beyond expressive capacity, by analyzing optimization bias and the learning dynamics.
AI.method: Analyze a minimal fixed-offset retrieval task; prove rotary encodings produce logit as function of relative offset; show absolute encodings leave out-of-range unconstrained; characterize as carrier kernel; derive attention-dilution law; perform linear-attention control; validate across seeds/offsets; extend to multi-layer/multi-head transformer.
AI.result: Exact equivariance reproduced at longer lengths; relative encodings generalize while absolute do not; deduce graceful accuracy decay; predictions borne out across settings; softmax-specific phenomenon; control experiments with linear attention show min-norm interpolant; results transfer to full-length generalization task.
AI.conclusion: Links the implicit biases in attention and extrapolation with the RASP-L conjecture; provides an optimization-based explanation for length generalization in transformers and a unifying view across recurrent and attention models.

title: Point Ladder Tuning: Parameter-Efficient Hierarchical Adaptation for 3D Point Cloud Understanding
summary: Fine-tuning pre-trained point-cloud backbones typically updates all parameters, resulting in substantial computation and memory overhead. More importantly, modern point backbones rely on aggressive tokenization and downsampling, which yields compact global tokens but irreversibly discards fine-grained local geometry, an inherent bottleneck for parameter-efficient adaptation. Consequently, existing PEFT methods that operate only on these coarsened tokens can modulate global semantics but struggle to recover the missing multi-scale locality. We present Point Ladder Tuning (PLT), a locality-aware PEFT framework that performs hierarchical, instance-conditioned adaptation while keeping the backbone frozen. PLT forms a lightweight closed loop: (i) a Hierarchical Ladder Network (HLN) constructs a multi-resolution local feature pyramid directly from raw points; (ii) a Local-Global Fusion (LGF) aligns and fuses local pyramids with intermediate backbone semantics; and (iii) a Dynamic Prompt Generator produces instance-aware multi-scale prompts to modulate the frozen backbone effectively. For dense prediction, we further introduce a lightweight segmentation head that progressively upsamples fused features and leverages backbone priors to refine fine structures. Extensive experiments on classification and dense prediction show that PLT consistently surpasses prior PEFT baselines with minimal tunable parameters. PLT achieves state-of-the-art performance using only 2.71% trainable parameters for classification and 7.69% for dense prediction, and scales favorably to larger backbones, requiring merely 0.36% parameters on PointGPT-L. The code is released at https://github.com/JunLinChang/ECCV2026-PLT.

AI.tldr: PLT introduces locality-aware PEFT for frozen point-cloud backbones by building a hierarchical local feature pyramid, fusing it with backbone semantics, and generating instance-aware prompts, achieving state-of-the-art results with minimal trainable parameters for both classification and dense prediction.
AI.motivation: Modern point-cloud backbones rely on aggressive tokenization and downsampling, which discard fine-grained local geometry. Existing PEFT methods acting on coarsened tokens struggle to recover multi-scale locality while keeping the backbone frozen; there is a need for locality-preserving, instance-conditioned adaptation with minimal parameter growth.
AI.method: 1) Hierarchical Ladder Network constructs a multi-resolution local feature pyramid from raw points. 2) Local-Global Fusion aligns and fuses local pyramids with intermediate backbone semantics. 3) Dynamic Prompt Generator produces instance-aware multi-scale prompts to modulate the frozen backbone. A lightweight segmentation head is added for dense prediction, progressively upsampling fused features with backbone priors.
AI.result: PLT consistently outperforms prior PEFT baselines on classification and dense prediction. It achieves state-of-the-art performance with only 2.71% trainable parameters for classification and 7.69% for dense prediction, and scales to larger backbones (e.g., PointGPT-L needing merely 0.36% trainable parameters). Code is released at the provided repository.
AI.conclusion: PLT enables efficient, locality-preserving adaptation of frozen point-cloud backbones through hierarchical, instance-conditioned prompts and multi-scale local fusion, delivering strong performance with minimal trainable parameters and favorable scalability.

title: Agents in the Wild: Where Research Meets Deployment
summary: Agentic systems large language model (LLM) based architectures capable of reasoning, planning, acting, and coordinating with tools and other agents are rapidly transitioning from research prototypes to production scale deployments across domains such as software engineering, scientific discovery, and finance. While academic work has emphasized benchmarks and algorithmic innovation, deployment raises new challenges around robustness, safety, and reliability. This tutorial brings together researchers and practitioners to explore advances in reasoning and planning, multi agent coordination, and evaluation, highlighting open challenges arising from deployment experience. Through applied case studies in pharmaceutical discovery and financial systems, we analyze common design patterns that make agentic systems successful, and discuss practical mitigation strategies for failure modes, such as verification pipelines, fallback mechanisms, and human in the loop supervision. Attendees will gain a comprehensive view of the field along with concrete design patterns, evaluation checklists, and templates for safe and reliable deployment across industries.

AI.tldr: A tutorial on deploying agentic LLM-based systems, highlighting robustness, safety, and reliability challenges and providing practical design patterns, evaluation checklists, and templates.
AI.motivation: As agentic LLMs move from research to production across domains, deployment raises new robustness, safety, and reliability challenges that require practical guidance and evaluation frameworks.
AI.method: A tutorial that combines reasoning and planning advances, multi-agent coordination, and evaluation with applied case studies in pharmaceutical discovery and financial systems, presenting common design patterns and mitigation strategies (verification pipelines, fallbacks, human-in-the-loop) and concrete templates.
AI.result: Participants gain concrete design patterns, evaluation checklists, and deployment templates, along with a clearer view of open challenges arising from deployment experience.
AI.conclusion: Sharing patterns and practical mitigations will advance safe, reliable deployment of agentic systems across industries.

title: Formulation-Level Auto-Tuning for QUBO-Based Machine Learning: A Case Study Across Multiple Quantum-Inspired Annealers
summary: This paper presents an Optuna-based formulation-level auto-tuning framework for support vector machines (SVMs) implemented on multiple quantum-inspired annealers. In an annealing-based SVM, continuous dual variables are discretized and converted into a quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) model. This transformation introduces three coupled classes of parameters: representation parameters-the encoding base B and bit depth K-which determine numerical range, resolution, and QUBO size; the RBF kernel parameter γ, which determines classifier geometry; and the equality-constraint penalty ξ, which controls feasibility and coefficient balance. We formulate their joint selection as a mixed discrete-continuous black-box optimization problem. The framework has two optimization levels: an inner annealer minimizes the generated QUBO, while an outer Optuna loop reconstructs the formulation in every trial and maximizes validation accuracy. The same solver-agnostic procedure is applied to Fixstars Amplify Annealing Engine, Toshiba SQBM+, and Fujitsu Digital Annealer using TPE and Gaussian-process samplers and is compared with conventional grid search. Experiments on linear and nonlinear classification tasks with 0-20% label noise show mean gains over grid search of approximately 0.8 and 2.1 percentage points, respectively. The results demonstrate that formulation quality and backend capability must be evaluated jointly and that task-level feedback can compensate for discretization, penalty imbalance, and backend-dependent approximate optimization.

AI.tldr: Optuna-based two-level auto-tuning for SVMs on quantum-inspired annealers; jointly optimizes representation (base B, bit depth K), kernel parameter γ, and equality-penalty ξ; yields ~0.8–2.1 percentage point gains vs grid search across multiple backends and noisy datasets.
AI.motivation: Address the challenge of joint formulation and hyperparameter selection in annealing-based SVMs; discretization and backend variability require co-optimization of data encoding, kernel geometry, and feasibility penalties.
AI.method: Two-level optimization: inner annealer minimizes QUBO; outer Optuna loop reconstructs the formulation per trial; uses TPE/GP samplers; applies across Fixstars Amplify, Toshiba SQBM+, Fujitsu Digital Annealer; compares to grid search.
AI.result: Mean accuracy gains ~0.8 and ~2.1 percentage points for linear and nonlinear tasks with 0-20% label noise; demonstrates that formulation quality and backend capability should be evaluated jointly; task-level feedback mitigates discretization and penalty imbalances.
AI.conclusion: Joint evaluation of formulation and backend is crucial; task-level feedback can compensate for discretization and backend approximations; suggests potential for generalization to other black-box solvers and integrative auto-tuning.

title: ABot-World-0: Infinite Interactive World Rollout on a Single Desktop GPU
summary: We present ABot-World-0, an action-conditioned video world model for real-time, long-horizon closed-loop interaction, supported by a multi-source data infrastructure spanning AAA games, simulation engines, and internet videos to learn controllable world dynamics. WorldExplorer performs agent-driven collection guided by training feedback, while a unified pipeline applies 14 deterministic quality checks, VLM-based assessment, and synchronized action and text annotation. We progressively distill a bidirectional action-conditioned teacher into a causal student through teacher forcing and ODE distillation, and introduce LongForcing to align long student self-rollouts with an extended-horizon teacher, mitigating accumulated distribution shift and autoregressive drift. Raw keyboard actions provide a unified control interface for scene roaming and third-person character interaction, while reference-character memory provides persistent appearance cues for identity consistency during third-person rollouts. For deployment, we co-design a streaming inference stack with a lightweight VAE decoder, efficient attention, memory-aware scheduling, and low-bit DiT inference. Across optimized low-bit configurations, ABot-World-0 streams 720P video at up to 16 FPS on a single NVIDIA RTX 5090 desktop GPU, with 1.2s action-to-first-frame latency and approximately 19GiB peak VRAM. Experiments on WorldRoamBench and extended interactive rollouts demonstrate competitive controllability and coherent long-horizon world evolution.

AI.tldr: ABot-World-0 is a real-time, action-conditioned video world model built from a multi-source data pipeline (AAA games, simulators, internet videos). It uses teacher–student distillation with LongForcing for long-horizon consistency, and a streaming, low-bit deployment stack achieving 720p at 16 FPS on RTX 5090 with ~1.2s latency and ~19 GiB VRAM. It demonstrates competitive controllability and coherent long-horizon evolution on WorldRoamBench.
AI.motivation: To enable controllable, long-horizon, real-time world modeling by integrating diverse data sources, robust quality checks, and efficient deployment, while mitigating distribution shift and autoregressive drift.
AI.method: Multi-source data infrastructure combining ABot WorldExplorer data collection guided by feedback; 14 deterministic quality checks; VLM-based assessment; synchronized action/text annotation; bidirectional action-conditioned teacher with causal student via ODE distillation; LongForcing to align long rollouts with extended-horizon teacher; raw keyboard actions as unified control; reference-character memory for identity consistency; streaming inference stack with lightweight VAE decoder, efficient attention, memory-aware scheduling, and low-bit DiT; hardware: 720p 16 FPS on RTX 5090, 1.2s latency, ~19 GiB VRAM.
AI.result: Experiments on WorldRoamBench and extended interactive rollouts show competitive controllability and coherent long-horizon world evolution.
AI.conclusion: ABot-World-0 demonstrates a scalable, real-time action-conditioned world model pipeline with robust long-horizon performance and practical deployment considerations.

title: CodeRescue: Budget-Calibrated Recovery Routing for Coding Agents
summary: Coding agents increasingly operate in executable environments where a failed attempt produces actionable feedback rather than merely an incorrect answer. Existing cost-aware systems typically treat such failures as cascade decisions: try a cheap model first, then escalate hard cases to a stronger and more expensive model. In coding, however, execution feedback can also make further cheap-model recovery worthwhile, raising a budgeted deployment question: when should an agent spend more cheap compute, and when should it escalate? We formulate this post-failure decision as recovery routing over heterogeneous actions and train a supervised router from execution rollouts. To make the same router usable under changing budgets, we add a Conformal Risk Control (CRC) layer that selects a deployment-time cost penalty without retraining and provides marginal expected-cost control under exchangeability. Across held-out failures from five coding benchmarks, cheap recovery and escalation exhibit complementary success patterns. The calibrated frontier improves over fixed actions, prompt-only routers, and a binary cascade baseline; in the main GPT-5.4-nano/GPT-5.4 setting, one CRC-calibrated frontier point exceeds always-escalate solve rate while using 35% of its mean recovery cost. Code is available at https://github.com/Qijia-He/agent-budget-control.

AI.tldr: A budget-aware recovery routing framework for coding agents using a supervised router and a conformal risk control layer to decide between cheap recovery vs escalation; yields calibrated, budget-robust performance gains across failures and benchmarks, surpassing baselines in a GPT-5.4-nano setting.
AI.motivation: In executable coding environments, failures provide actionable feedback and create opportunities for cheap recovery. Traditional cascade approaches only escalate when cheap options fail, but do not exploit post-failure recovery opportunities, especially under shifting budgets.
AI.method: Train a supervised router on execution rollouts to route between heterogeneous actions (cheap recovery vs escalation); integrate a Conformal Risk Control (CRC) layer to select deployment-time cost penalties without retraining and to provide marginal expected-cost control under exchangeability; evaluate on five coding benchmarks, comparing against fixed-action, prompt-only routers, and a binary cascade baseline.
AI.result: A calibrated frontier (CRC) improves over baselines, with one frontier point in the GPT-5.4-nano/GPT-5.4 setting exceeding the always-escalate solve rate while using only about 35% of the mean recovery cost.
AI.conclusion: Budget-aware recovery routing with CRC enables dynamic, cost-efficient use of cheap recovery paths and escalation across changing budgets, achieving better trade-offs without retraining; the approach generalizes to budget shifts and shows strong practical gains; code is available at the referenced repository.

title: PertReason: A Knowledge-Grounded Benchmark and Framework for Cell-State-Conditioned Mechanistic Reasoning of Perturbation Effects
comment: Preprint; 31 pages; Dongkwan Kim and Yiming Gao contributed equally to this work
summary: Evaluating machine learning in scientific domains requires separating correct predictions from correct reasons under realistic distribution shifts. We introduce PertReason, a knowledge-grounded benchmark and framework suite for cell-state--conditioned reasoning about perturbation effects. At its core, PertReasonQA is a benchmark that tests whether models can generate mechanistically faithful explanations while remaining robust to complex shifts, such as new cells and unseen perturbations. PertReasonQA combines single-cell genetic and chemical perturbation data across multiple cellular contexts with knowledge graphs, and dynamically conditions pathways on cell-specific basal states to avoid generic memorization. Evaluations on state-of-the-art models reveal systematic gaps between predictive accuracy and mechanistic reasoning. Specifically, these models exhibit failure modes largely invisible to standard benchmarks, such as deriving correct answers through flawed logic, ignoring cellular context, and generating directionally inconsistent mechanisms. As a reference probe of the benchmark, we present PertReasonLM, a large language model trained to align outcome predictions with context-specific mechanistic reasoning. Our model targets the identified failure modes by grounding rationales in context-specific pathways and tightening agreement between outcomes and mechanisms. Together, we provide a diagnostic framework for exposing and mitigating failures in faithful reasoning in data-rich scientific systems.

AI.tldr: PertReason introduces a knowledge-grounded benchmark and framework to evaluate cell-state conditioned reasoning about perturbations, featuring PertReasonQA (mechanistically faithful explanations under distribution shifts) and PertReasonLM (alignment of outcomes with mechanisms). It reveals gaps between predictive accuracy and mechanistic reasoning in current models and provides a diagnostic framework to mitigate faithful reasoning failures in data-rich biological systems.
AI.motivation: Evaluate machine learning in scientific domains beyond accuracy, by separating correct predictions from mechanistically faithful explanations under realistic distribution shifts, and to prevent reliance on memorization by incorporating context-specific biological knowledge.
AI.method: Construct PertReasonQA by integrating single-cell genetic and chemical perturbation data across multiple cellular contexts with knowledge graphs, dynamically conditioning pathways on cell-specific basal states; evaluate state-of-the-art models for mechanistic fidelity. Introduce PertReasonLM, a large language model trained to align outcome predictions with context-specific mechanistic reasoning by grounding rationales in pathways and tightening agreement between outcomes and mechanisms.
AI.result: Empirical evaluations show systematic gaps between predictive accuracy and mechanistic reasoning; models can derive correct answers via flawed logic, ignore cellular context, or produce directionally inconsistent mechanisms. PertReasonLM is shown as a reference probe that improves alignment between predictions and mechanistic explanations.
AI.conclusion: PertReason provides a diagnostic framework to expose and mitigate failures in faithful reasoning in data-rich scientific systems, with PertReasonLM serving as a baseline to improve grounding of rationales in biology.

title: Anatomy-Aware 3D Mesh Refinement of Pericardium Segmentations on Computed Tomography
comment: This preprint has not undergone peer review (when applicable) or any post-submission improvements or corrections. The Version of Record of this contribution is published in the proceedings for MIUA 2026
summary: Accurate delineation of the pericardium in a cardiac CT scan is essential for quantifying epicardial adipose tissue, yet it remains one of the most challenging structures to segment due to its poor contrast boundaries. Instead of solely relying on image gradients, our framework leverages the anatomical context of surrounding anatomical structures to guide the segmentation. This work introduces a novel 3D iterative mesh refinement framework that balances anatomical and geometric forces derived from inherent anatomical rules to refine an initial, possibly ambiguous, segmentation into a high-precision, anatomically plausible result. Designed as a model-agnostic post-processing step, our method uses a 3D vector field to iteratively push the vertices to the correct anatomical locations. Evaluating the refinement on both a high-resolution in-house dataset and a coarse, sparsely annotated open-source dataset, our method consistently improves all volumetric, surface, and anatomical metrics. The framework demonstrates greater improvement when applied to weaker initial segmentations, highlighting its potential for improving segmentations for out-of-domain models and in limited-training-data scenarios. The method is formulated as a gradient-based, GPU-accelerated framework that can be easily extended to other anatomical use cases.

AI.tldr: A model-agnostic 3D iterative mesh refinement post-process improves pericardium segmentation in cardiac CT by combining anatomical and geometric cues via a 3D vector-field-driven mesh refinement, with GPU acceleration, improving accuracy especially for weak initial segmentations.
AI.motivation: Pericardium delineation is hard due to poor contrast boundaries; leverages surrounding anatomical context and geometric priors to produce anatomically plausible results; aims to help out-of-domain models and data-limited scenarios.
AI.method: 3D iterative mesh refinement framework that uses a 3D vector field to iteratively move mesh vertices; balances anatomical and geometric forces derived from anatomical rules; acts as a model-agnostic post-processing step; GPU-accelerated and extensible to other anatomical use cases.
AI.result: Evaluated on a high-resolution in-house dataset and a coarse, sparsely annotated open-source dataset; shows consistent improvements across volumetric, surface, and anatomical metrics; larger gains for weaker initial segmentations, indicating robustness to poor inputs and usefulness for out-of-domain models or limited data.
AI.conclusion: The framework provides accurate, anatomically plausible pericardium segmentation as a post-processing refinement and is readily transferable to other anatomical segmentation tasks, combining anatomical priors with geometric refinement in a GPU-accelerated pipeline.

title: QScheduler: Adaptive Gradient Sampling for Zeroth-Order On-Device Training on INT8 NPUs
summary: Zeroth-Order (ZO) optimization enables On-Device Learning (ODL) on NPU-equipped microcontrollers by estimating gradients through forward passes alone, bypassing the need for backpropagation primitives and reducing memory requirements. The number of gradient samples q critically affects training: insufficient samples produce noisy gradients that plateau early, while excessive samples consume more computational resources. However, finding an optimal q typically requires costly hyperparameter searches. This work introduces QScheduler, an adaptive algorithm that adjusts q based on training progress, and provides the first proof-of-concept of INT8 quantized on-device training on the STM32N6's Neural-ART NPU. Experiments on EuroSAT and STL-10 show that QScheduler matches well-tuned fixed-q configurations for both ResNet18 and MobileNetV2, without requiring prior q hyperparameter optimization.

AI.tldr: Adaptive zero-order gradient sampling (QScheduler) tunes gradient-sample count q during on-device training, matching fixed-q performance without hyperparameter search, demonstrated with INT8 quantized training on STM32N6 Neural-ART NPU.
AI.motivation: Zero-order optimization enables on-device learning on resource-constrained microcontrollers but requires choosing the number of gradient samples q. Too few samples yield noisy gradients; too many waste computation. Hyperparameter search for q is costly on-device.
AI.method: Introduce QScheduler, an adaptive algorithm that adjusts q based on training progress. Provide a proof-of-concept of INT8 quantized on-device training on the STM32N6's Neural-ART NPU. Evaluate on EuroSAT and STL-10 with ResNet18 and MobileNetV2.
AI.result: QScheduler matches well-tuned fixed-q configurations for both ResNet18 and MobileNetV2 on EuroSAT and STL-10 datasets.
AI.conclusion: Adaptive q scheduling enables effective on-device ZO training without prior q hyperparameter optimization and demonstrates feasibility of INT8 on-device training on the STM32N6 Neural-ART NPU; broader hardware applicability and datasets remain for future work.

title: IGGT4D: Streaming 4D Instance-Grounded Geometry Transformer
summary: Real-world spatial intelligence requires agents to understand scenes from continuous video streams, where objects move, persist, disappear, and reappear over time. While recent spatial foundation models have enabled generalizable feed-forward 3D reconstruction, most streaming methods remain geometry-centric and lack temporally consistent object-level understanding. Meanwhile, existing semantic reconstruction and 3D-aware vision-language methods largely rely on externally extracted 2D semantic cues or loosely coupled geometry inputs, limiting unified geometry-instance learning in long dynamic scenes. In this paper, we propose IGGT4D, a streaming instance-grounded geometry Transformer for online 4D scene understanding. IGGT4D processes video frames sequentially, reuses historical context through causal spatial-temporal modeling, and incrementally updates a unified representation of camera motion, geometry, and object identity. This enables long-sequence feed-forward reconstruction with geometry-instance consistency in dynamic environments. To address the lack of high-quality 4D supervision, we further construct InsScene4D-147K, a large-scale dataset spanning real/synthetic and static/dynamic scenes, with RGB images, depth, poses, and temporally consistent instance masks generated by an automated geometry-guided annotation pipeline. Experiments on 3D reconstruction, pose estimation, instance spatial tracking, and open-vocabulary segmentation demonstrate that IGGT4D outperforms existing streaming baselines while maintaining scalable online inference for long dynamic sequences.

AI.tldr: IGGT4D is a streaming, instance-grounded geometry Transformer for online 4D scene understanding, achieving geometry-instance consistency over long dynamic sequences; enabled by InsScene4D-147K dataset.
AI.motivation: Real-world streaming 3D reconstruction is geometry-centric and lacks temporally consistent object-level semantics; existing semantic or 3D-aware methods rely on external 2D cues or loosely coupled inputs, hindering unified geometry-instance learning in long dynamic scenes.
AI.method: IGGT4D processes frames sequentially with causal spatial-temporal modeling, reusing historical context; incrementally updates a unified representation of camera motion, geometry, and object identity; accompanied by InsScene4D-147K dataset with RGB, depth, poses, and temporally consistent instance masks obtained via automated geometry-guided annotation.
AI.result: Outperforms existing streaming baselines on 3D reconstruction, pose estimation, instance spatial tracking, and open-vocabulary segmentation; demonstrates scalable online inference for long dynamic sequences.
AI.conclusion: Demonstrates feasibility of online geometry-instance learning in 4D scenes and introduces a large-scale dataset to support it; establishes IGGT4D as a state-of-the-art streaming solution for long dynamic environments.

title: Elicitation without Backpropagation: Steering Model Behavior by Optimizing the Latent Posterior
summary: In the \emph{latent posterior model} of transformer behavior, the next-token distribution arises from a posterior over latent predictive models conditioned on the context, mixed to generate continuations. We exploit this model in settings where it is exact, namely Bayes-filtered transformers (BFTs) meta-learned on sequences from a hierarchical prior, to introduce \textbf{Posterior Prefix Tuning (PPT)}, a new method for \emph{eliciting} behavior from a transformer: given a utility function on continuations, find a prompt under which the transformer generates continuations of high expected utility. For a BFT, the elicitation objective factors through the latent posterior, and the gradient of this objective can be estimated from samples of the prior alone. PPT optimizes the parameters of a distribution over hard prompts: it draws prior samples once from the BFT via predictive Monte Carlo (PMC), then estimates the gradient by importance sampling against them. The optimization performs no transformer forward passes and no backpropagation through the transformer, and the prior samples are utility-independent, so a single set of samples drives elicitation against any number of utilities at negligible marginal cost. We validate PPT on Beta--Bernoulli and reinforced urn BFTs across three utility families (reverse cross-entropy, frequency matching, Dyck validity).

AI.tldr: Posterior Prefix Tuning (PPT) elicits transformer behavior by optimizing a distribution over hard prompts under a latent posterior model, using predictive Monte Carlo samples from a Bayes-filtered transformer. Gradients are estimated via importance sampling, requiring no transformer forward passes or backprop, and a single prior sample set supports multiple utility objectives. Validated on Beta–Bernoulli and reinforced-urn BFTs across multiple utilities.
AI.motivation: To enable efficient, principled elicitation of high-utility continuations from transformers by exploiting exact Bayes-filtered transformer posteriors and reusing a common set of prior samples to handle diverse utility objectives at negligible marginal cost.
AI.method: Posterior Prefix Tuning (PPT) optimizes a distribution over hard prompts. It draws prior samples once from a Bayes-filtered transformer (BFT) via predictive Monte Carlo (PMC) and estimates the gradient of the elicitation objective with respect to prompt-distribution parameters using importance sampling against those samples. The elicitation objective factors through the latent posterior; the process requires no transformer forward passes and no backpropagation through the transformer; prior samples are utility-independent, enabling queries for any number of utilities with a single sample set.
AI.result: Empirical validation on Beta–Bernoulli and reinforced urn BFTs across three utility families (reverse cross-entropy, frequency matching, Dyck validity) demonstrates PPT can meaningfully elicit high-utility continuations while incurring negligible marginal cost per additional utility.
AI.conclusion: PPT provides a low-cost, principled elicitation framework within exact BFTs by leveraging latent posteriors and a fixed set of prior samples; it decouples prompting from downstream utility evaluation and avoids direct transformer optimization. Extensions to larger models and real-world tasks, and analysis of sensitivity to prior choice and utility mis-specification, are warranted.

title: PathAgentBench: Benchmarking Evidence-Seeking Vision-Language Models on Whole-Slide Pathology Image
summary: Whole-slide image (WSI) diagnosis requires identifying diagnostically relevant regions, examining them across magnifications, and integrating multi-scale evidence. However, most existing pathology benchmarks evaluate models on pre-cropped patches or pre-extracted slide features, leaving their ability to acquire evidence directly from gigapixel WSIs largely untested. We introduce PathAgentBench, a benchmark for evaluating evidence-seeking vision-language models (VLMs) across four complementary capabilities: image-to-text matching for evidence interpretation, text-to-image retrieval for evidence verification, diagnostic-region localization for evidence acquisition, and multi-scale reasoning for evidence integration. The benchmark is organized as a diagnostic tree that links nested regions across magnifications with scale-specific findings and path-level diagnoses. It contains 1,822 TCGA WSIs and 17,135 diagnostic paths annotated by ten board-certified pathologists. An additional private cohort of 190 breast cancer WSIs with detailed annotations is used to evaluate autonomous whole-slide exploration. We evaluate 20 general-purpose, medical, and pathology-specialized models. Leading open-weight models achieve over 93% accuracy in multi-scale reasoning and over 50% accuracy in both cross-modal matching tasks. In contrast, diagnostic-region localization remains challenging: the best text-guided mean intersection-over-union is below 0.09, underperforming a simple center-based heuristic. During autonomous exploration, the unconditional hit rate decreases from 0.522 at low magnification to 0.185 at intermediate magnification and 0.020 at high magnification. These results reveal a pronounced gap between reasoning over curated evidence and acquiring that evidence directly from WSIs. PathAgentBench provides a unified framework for measuring and improving evidence-seeking pathology models.

AI.tldr: PathAgentBench evaluates evidence-seeking capabilities of vision-language models on whole-slide pathology, focusing on multi-scale reasoning, cross-modal evidence matching, region localization, and autonomous exploration across gigapixel WSIs.
AI.motivation: Address the gap between traditional patch-based evaluation and the ability to acquire evidence directly from WSIs, by providing a unified benchmark that tests multi-scale, evidence-seeking behavior in pathology VLMs.
AI.method: Construct a diagnostic tree linking nested regions across magnifications with scale-specific findings and path-level diagnoses. Use 1,822 TCGA WSIs with 17,135 diagnostic paths annotated by 10 pathologists, plus a private cohort of 190 breast cancer WSIs. Evaluate 20 models on four tasks: image-to-text matching, text-to-image retrieval, diagnostic-region localization (text-guided), and multi-scale reasoning; additionally assess autonomous exploration with fixed magnification strategies.
AI.result: Leading open-weight models achieve >93% accuracy in multi-scale reasoning and >50% in cross-modal matching tasks; diagnostic-region localization is poor (text-guided mean IoU < 0.09). In autonomous exploration, hit rates fall from 0.522 at low magnification to 0.185 (intermediate) and 0.020 (high).
AI.conclusion: There is a substantial gap between the ability to reason over curated evidence and to autonomously acquire relevant evidence from WSIs. PathAgentBench provides a unified framework to measure and improve evidence-seeking pathology models.

title: Countercurrent Multiplier Networks: A Renal-Inspired Iterative Operator with Provably Bounded Fixed-Point Dynamics
summary: The mammalian kidney concentrates urine using a mechanism with no analogue in current neural architectures: the countercurrent multiplier. Two anti-parallel flows joined at a hairpin recirculate a weak magnitude-bounded local pump into a large axial gradient achieving a four-fold concentration increase from a single-effect gradient that never exceeds 200 mOsm at any point. We formalize this mechanism as a differentiable sequence operator the Countercurrent Multiplier (CCM) layer and study it as an alternative to residual iterative refinement.

AI.tldr: Introduces the Countercurrent Multiplier (CCM) layer, a differentiable sequence operator that emulates a kidney-like countercurrent mechanism to amplify gradients, proposed as an alternative to residual iterative refinement.
AI.motivation: Biological countercurrent multiplication achieves substantial concentration from modest local gradients, a capability not mirrored in current neural architectures. The work formalizes this into a differentiable operator to enable more efficient, powerful gradient amplification in neural networks.
AI.method: Formalize the mechanism as a differentiable CCM layer composed of two anti-parallel flows with hairpin recirculation and a weak local pump, producing a large axial gradient from a within-bound gradient (never exceeding 200 mOsm). The CCM layer is studied as an alternative to standard residual iterative refinement.
AI.result: The CCM layer is developed and analyzed as a novel differentiable sequence operator; the work frames it as an alternative to residual iterative refinement, outlining theoretical properties and potential benefits, but no explicit empirical results are provided in the abstract.
AI.conclusion: The CCM layer offers a biologically inspired, differentiable sequence operator that can potentially improve gradient amplification efficiency and reduce reliance on iterative refinement, warranting further empirical evaluation and integration into neural architectures.

title: From Trajectories to Instructions: Language-Conditioned Meta-Reinforcement Learning
comment: Accepted at the International Conference on Artificial Neural Networks (ICANN 2026)
summary: Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning (MAML) is a widely used framework for reinforcement learning (RL) that enables efficient transfer by learning global policy parameters that can be rapidly adapted to new tasks. MAML training proceeds in two loops: an inner loop where the global parameters are adapted to task-specific parameters, and an outer loop where these task-specific parameters are evaluated and losses are back-propagated to improve the global parameters. Traditionally, the inner loop adaptation is performed by collecting trajectories from the task environment and applying gradient updates on the empirical expected return, which can be a costly operation. We note that it is the outer loop that drives the actual learning of global parameters, and therefore the inner loop adaptation mechanism need not be restricted to be gradient-based. This observation leads us to ask: Can we replace the inner loop trajectory collection and gradient update with a simpler, task-specific signal? In many practical settings, tasks are naturally accompanied by language instructions. Leveraging these instructions as a direct task-specific signal, we propose LA-MAML (Language Adapted MAML), which modifies the inner loop by adapting the global policy parameters in a single step through a learned embedding of the task instruction, replacing the inner loop trajectory collection and gradient-based updates. Experiments on the BabyAI benchmark demonstrate that LA-MAML achieves competitive or improved performance compared to baselines at a significantly lower per-iteration wall-clock training time. These results demonstrate that language instructions are an effective and efficient substitute for trajectory-based inner loop adaptation in meta RL.

AI.tldr: LA-MAML replaces the inner-loop gradient adaptation in MAML for RL with a single-step adaptation guided by a learned embedding of language instructions, achieving competitive performance with much lower wall-clock time on BabyAI.
AI.motivation: Inner-loop trajectory collection and gradient updates in MAML-based RL are costly; aim to reduce computational burden by using task-specific signals (language instructions) as a direct adaptation signal.
AI.method: Introduce a language-conditioned inner loop that computes a one-step adaptation of the global policy using an embedding of the instruction; no trajectory-based inner updates; training evaluates outer loop with standard MAML objective.
AI.result: LA-MAML attains competitive or improved performance relative to baselines on BabyAI and significantly reduces per-iteration wall-clock training time.
AI.conclusion: Language instructions can serve as an effective and efficient substitute for trajectory-based inner loop adaptation in meta-RL, suggesting broader utility of language-conditioned signals for fast policy adaptation.

title: ERank in Latent Space as an Image-Complexity and Richness Measure
summary: We propose the effective rank (ERank) of the channel covariance of an image's deep feature map as a per-sample, label-free measure of visual richness, computed from a single forward pass through a frozen pretrained encoder. ERank counts how many decorrelated channel directions an image activates, and we characterize its properties, including its behavior under noise. Empirically, ERank orders images from plain to visually rich, correlates with codec bitrate, sharpness, and edge density, and correlates with human complexity annotations on IC9600 with $r = 0.72$. As a data-selection criterion, removing low-ERank samples improves super-resolution and removing high-ERank samples improves OCR, in both pretraining and finetuning, while selection does not help classification, segmentation, or denoising. ERank is thus a cheap richness signal, useful exactly when task difficulty is governed by input richness.

AI.tldr: ERank provides a per-image, label-free measure of visual richness based on the effective rank of the channel covariance in a frozen encoder's feature map. It orders images by richness, correlates with bitrate, sharpness, and edge density, and can guide data selection to improve certain tasks (e.g., SR when sampling low-ERank; OCR when sampling high-ERank) but not for others (classification/segmentation/denoising).
AI.motivation: To quantify image visual richness cheaply and without labels, enabling data selection and understanding of how input complexity affects downstream tasks.
AI.method: Compute the effective rank of the channel covariance of a single layer of a frozen pretrained encoder's feature map for each image. Analyze noise behavior and empirical correlations; validate on IC9600 with human complexity annotations (r=0.72).
AI.result: ERank orders images from plain to rich; correlates with codec bitrate, sharpness, edge density; correlation with human complexity r=0.72; data-selection based on ERank improves downstream tasks: remove low-ERank improves super-resolution; remove high-ERank improves OCR; no improvement for classification, segmentation, or denoising.
AI.conclusion: ERank is a cheap, task-relevant richness signal when input complexity governs task difficulty, offering a practical tool for data curation in pretraining/finetuning pipelines.

title: ABOPD: Antibody CDR Design via On-Policy Distillation
summary: Antibodies are essential therapeutic molecules, and their complementarity-determining regions (CDRs) form the primary antigen-recognition interface. Recent protein generative models have demonstrated broad capabilities in biomolecular design, yet post-training strategies for downstream objectives remain limited. Standard denoising training operates on noisy states obtained by perturbing native structures, whereas recursive generation proceeds through model-generated intermediate states. For flexible antibody CDR loops such as CDR-H3, this mismatch can allow backbone deviations to accumulate along the denoising trajectory and compromise antigen-facing loop geometry. We introduce ABOPD, an antibody design framework based on on-policy distillation that leverages privileged native geometry during training to supervise states visited along the model's own denoising trajectories. With this fine-grained structural supervision, ABOPD substantially improves structural recovery on RAbD CDR-H3 generation, reducing RMSD by 0.42 Å (from 2.37 Å to 1.95 Å) and outperforming supervised fine-tuning and offline distillation controls, offering a path to higher-fidelity protein design.

AI.tldr: ABOPD uses on-policy distillation with privileged native geometry to supervise denoising trajectories in antibody design, achieving higher fidelity CDR-H3 structures.
AI.motivation: Mismatch between denoising training on perturbed native states and recursive generation can allow backbone deviations to accumulate in flexible CDR-H3 loops, compromising antigen-binding geometry.
AI.method: An antibody design framework ABOPD that employs on-policy distillation leveraging privileged native geometry during training to supervise states along the model's denoising trajectory.
AI.result: RMSD for RAbD CDR-H3 generation reduced from 2.37 Å to 1.95 Å (0.42 Å improvement); ABOPD outperforms supervised fine-tuning and offline distillation controls.
AI.conclusion: On-policy distillation with privileged geometry yields higher-fidelity antibody designs and provides a path to improved downstream objectives in protein design.

title: InstructMixup: Instruction-Guided Salient Patch Editing for Robust Data Augmentation
summary: In image and video technologies, data augmentation is widely used to improve the generalization of deep visual models, and mixup-based strategies that interpolate between samples have become the dominant approach. However, computing informative mixing regions adds substantial overhead, and blending content across different images frequently disrupts the semantic integrity of the resulting sample. We propose \our{}, a data augmentation method that constructs challenging yet label-consistent training samples entirely within a single visual sample. \our{} first extracts multi-scale salient patches from the sample using a lightweight saliency detector, refines each patch with an instruction-guided generative model, and blends the edited patch back into the non-salient regions of the same sample; because the generative edits are computed once and cached offline, this step adds negligible training cost. To further diversify the learned representation, \our{} injects self-similar fractal structure into the same salient regions at an adaptive ratio, so each training sample carries both fractal and non-fractal structure. We derive a second-order approximation of the resulting vicinal risk, showing that the method simultaneously enforces invariance to the generative edit and suppresses curvature along the perturbed salient directions, and we verify both predictions empirically. We evaluate on small to large backbones for instance Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Vision Transformers (ViTs) and Vision-Language Foundational Models (VLMs) across seven benchmarks covering coarse- and fine-grained classification, robustness to corruption and occlusion, calibration, and transfer and self-supervised learning, InstructMixup outperforms nine competing augmentation methods, surpassing the strongest baseline across all benchmarks.

AI.tldr: InstructMixup: a single-sample, within-image augmentation that edits salient patches with an instruction-guided generator and injects fractal self-similarity, achieving label-consistent, cost-efficient augmentation and robust generalization.
AI.motivation: Traditional mixup-based augmentations either mix content across images (costly and semantically risky) or rely on within-image edits that may still be limited. The method aims to maximize data diversity and robustness while preserving label fidelity and keeping computational overhead low by reusing cached edits.
AI.method: 1) Identify multi-scale salient patches in each image using a lightweight saliency detector. 2) Refine patches with an instruction-guided generative model. 3) Blend edited patches back into the non-salient regions of the same image. 4) Cache the edits offline to incur negligible runtime cost. 5) Inject adaptive self-similar fractal structure into salient regions. 6) Derive and validate a second-order vicinal-risk approximation showing invariance to edits and reduced curvature along perturbed directions.
AI.result: Evaluated across seven benchmarks on CNNs, ViTs, and VLMs for tasks including coarse/fine classification, robustness, calibration, transfer, and self-supervised learning. InstructMixup consistently outperforms nine competing augmentations and surpasses the strongest baseline across benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: Within-image, label-consistent augmentation with cached generative edits and adaptive fractal perturbations yields strong generalization and robustness gains, supported by theoretical vicinal-risk analysis and extensive empirical validation across diverse architectures and tasks.

title: Regime-Aware Physics-Guided Early Warning of Lithium-Ion Battery Thermal Runaway Using Thermo-Mechanical Signals
summary: Thermal runaway in lithium-ion batteries poses a major safety risk to electric vehicles and energy storage systems. Current early-warning methods depend mainly on temperature and may therefore miss mechanical precursors that emerge before rapid heating. We introduce a regime-aware, physics-guided framework that integrates temperature, voltage, force, deformation, and state-of-charge measurements for early warning under controlled mechanical abuse. A lightweight convolutional classifier first infers safe, warning, or danger regimes from mechanical signals. These regime estimates then condition a causal temporal convolutional backbone through feature-wise linear modulation, physics-biased attention, and regime-dependent gating. Joint learning unifies regime identification, thermal-runaway detection, and time-to-disaster estimation. We evaluate the framework using leave-one-experiment-out cross-validation on 30 mechanical-abuse tests across state-of-charge levels of 10%, 50%, and 90% and two loading protocols. The method achieves an F1 score of 0.89, a high-temperature prediction root-mean-square error of 12.3 °C, a mean warning lead time of 15.6 s, a detection success rate of 0.92, and an experiment-level false alarm rate of 2.7%. Its lead time exceeds that of the strongest baseline by 69.6%. Removing force reduces the lead time by 60.3%, highlighting the value of mechanical precursors. These results support regime-aware thermo-mechanical fusion as a promising strategy for earlier and more reliable thermal-runaway warning under controlled abuse conditions.

AI.tldr: A regime-aware, physics-guided multi-sensor framework for early thermal-runaway warning in Li-ion cells under mechanical abuse; achieves high F1, low RMSE, and substantial lead time by conditioning a temporal backbone on inferred regimes.
AI.motivation: Current early-warning approaches rely mainly on temperature and may miss mechanical precursors; detecting thermo-mechanical precursors under controlled mechanical abuse improves safety for EVs and energy storage systems.
AI.method: A two-stage model: (1) a lightweight convolutional classifier infers safe, warning, or danger regimes from mechanical signals; (2) regime estimates condition a causal temporal convolutional backbone via feature-wise linear modulation (FiLM), physics-biased attention, and regime-dependent gating. Joint learning optimizes regime identification, thermal-runaway detection, and time-to-disaster estimation. Evaluation uses leave-one-experiment-out cross-validation on 30 mechanical-abuse tests across SOC levels of 10%, 50%, and 90% with two loading protocols.
AI.result: F1 = 0.89; high-temperature RMSE = 12.3 °C; mean warning lead time = 15.6 s; detection success rate = 0.92; experiment-level false alarm rate = 2.7%. Lead time exceeds strongest baseline by 69.6%. Ablation: removing force reduces lead time by 60.3%.
AI.conclusion: Regime-aware thermo-mechanical fusion is a promising strategy for earlier and more reliable thermal-runaway warning under controlled abuse conditions.

title: OmniReasoner: Thinking with Long Audio-Video via Native Tool Use
summary: Long audio-video reasoning is difficult for omnimodal LLMs because the decisive evidence is often sparse, cross-modal, and too expensive to preserve with uniformly high-fidelity inputs. We introduce OmniReasoner, a tool-use post-training framework for Thinking with Long Audio-Video: omni-modal LLMs learn, via supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, to decide whether and where to call a zoom-in tool before answering. OmniReasoner first builds a low-cost global preview of the full stream and then, when needed, calls the zoom-in tool with a requested temporal interval for higher-fidelity visual and audio inspection before answering. Because the model observes different sampling granularities before and after this call -- a sparse global preview and a denser local clip -- we introduce TimeAnchor, which keeps the tool's temporal argument valid and round-trip-consistent across these granularities, rather than tied to frame indices from a particular sampling rate. To make this tool-use behavior trainable without expensive manual interval annotation, we build a Temporal Augmented Data Engine that synthesizes tool-use post-training trajectories by video editing and composition. Experiments across omnimodal and video benchmarks show that OmniReasoner improves both answer accuracy and temporal grounding while concentrating high-fidelity computation on informative regions. Code is available at https://github.com/RockyChen0205/OmniReasoner.

AI.tldr: OmniReasoner enables an omnimodal LLM to strategically call a zoom-in tool for long audio-video reasoning by learning when and where to inspect high-fidelity clips, using TimeAnchor to maintain cross-granularity consistency and a Temporal Augmented Data Engine to train tool-use trajectories. This yields better accuracy and temporal grounding while focusing expensive computation on informative regions.
AI.motivation: Long audio-video reasoning is difficult because decisive evidence is sparse, cross-modal, and costly to preserve at uniform high fidelity. A mechanism to selectively obtain high-fidelity evidence is needed to improve accuracy and efficiency.
AI.method: The framework first builds a low-cost global preview of the full stream. It then decides when and where to call a zoom-in tool with a requested temporal interval for higher-fidelity inspection before answering. TimeAnchor ensures the tool’s temporal argument remains valid across different sampling granularities. A Temporal Augmented Data Engine synthesizes tool-use training trajectories via video editing and composition, enabling trainable supervision without manual interval annotation. Training uses supervised fine-tuning plus reinforcement learning.
AI.result: Experiments on omnimodal and video benchmarks show improved answer accuracy and better temporal grounding, with high-fidelity computation concentrated on informative regions.
AI.conclusion: OmniReasoner provides an effective, trainable tool-use framework for long audio-video reasoning, balancing accuracy and efficiency; code is available at the authors’ GitHub.

title: HindsightBench: A Black-Box Behavioral Audit Protocol for Parametric Hindsight in Time-Indexed LLM Decision Tasks
comment: 15 pages, 3 figures. Code, panel, and per-model audit rows: https://github.com/Khaozhe/hindsightbench (v1.0 release archived at doi:10.5281/zenodo.21453191)
summary: Large language models leak parametric knowledge of realized outcomes into historical financial decision tasks. Existence is settled; what users lack is a cheap way to audit a given model for it. We present HindsightBench, a black-box behavioral audit protocol that profiles parametric hindsight in any time-indexed LLM decision task at probe-level cost (no backtests, no logprobs, no corpus access). The protocol chains a four-arm date-manipulation matrix (revealed/date-only/masked/transplanted), dual memory probes (date recovery; outcome recall), and six per-model metrics -- trigger strength, transplant effect, post-cutoff placebo, recoverability, behaviorally effective knowledge cutoff, and a recall-accuracy dissociation coefficient -- with explicit gates where identifiability is data-dependent. Applying it to 15 models from seven vendors on a 258-node vintage-correct macro panel yields three headline patterns: (i) the date-trigger reflex tracks training generation, not scale -- absent across the 2024 open-weight generation from 1B to 70B, present in every tested 2026-generation model, and switching on within one vendor lineage (Qwen3 -> Qwen3.6) at fixed MoE architecture and 3B active parameters; (ii) effective cutoffs span 22 months across vendors and precede vendor-reported dates by up to eight months, invalidating calendar-window placebo designs; (iii) audit results are not invariant to serving -- BF16 serving of an FP8-referenced model breaks the trigger estimate's stability while AWQ-INT4 preserves it, and a provider-locked reasoning regime makes one probe non-convergent -- so the protocol ships with operational requirements (pin quantization and thinking regime; disclose parser and sampling policy). We release the panel, frozen preregistrations, per-model audit rows with measured dollar costs, transcripts, and one-command regeneration.

AI.tldr: HindsightBench is a black-box behavioral audit protocol for auditing parametric hindsight in time-indexed LLM decision tasks, using a four-arm date-manipulation matrix, dual memory probes, and six per-model metrics. Applied to 15 models from seven vendors on a 258-node macro panel, it uncovers trends linking training-generation to date-trigger behavior, nontrivial hidden-cutoffs preceding vendor dates, and strong sensitivity to serving regimes; and provides operational requirements and released artifacts for replication.
AI.motivation: To cheaply and model-agnostically audit parametric knowledge leakage about realized outcomes in LLMs without backtests, per-model logs, or corpus access.
AI.method: Four-arm date-manipulation matrix (revealed, date-only, masked, transplanted); dual memory probes (date recovery; outcome recall); six metrics (trigger strength, transplant effect, post-cutoff placebo, recoverability, behaviorally effective knowledge cutoff, recall-accuracy dissociation); explicit data-dependent gates for identifiability; applied to 15 models from seven vendors on a 258-node macro panel; operational constraints include pin quantization and thinking regime, with parser and sampling policy disclosure.
AI.result: Three headline patterns: (i) date-trigger reflex tracks training generation rather than model scale, present in 2026-generation models but absent in 2024 open-weight generation (1B–70B) and switching on within a vendor lineage (Qwen3 → Qwen3.6) under fixed MoE and 3B active parameters; (ii) effective cutoffs span about 22 months across vendors and precede vendor-reported dates by up to eight months, invalidating calendar-window placebo designs; (iii) results vary with serving: BF16 FP8 breaks trigger stability while AWQ-INT4 preserves it; provider-locked reasoning regime can render one probe non-convergent; protocol provides operational requirements and disclosures; release includes the panel, preregistrations, per-model audit rows with costs, transcripts, and one-command regeneration.
AI.conclusion: The protocol offers a practical, data-dependent auditing framework for parametric hindsight with explicit identifiability constraints, demonstrating nontrivial leakage in a time-indexed setting. It highlights sensitivity to deployment choices and calendar-based baselines, and provides artifacts to support replication and policy in model auditing.

title: ExpertVerse: A General-Purpose Benchmark for Expert-Level Reasoning in Knowledge-Intensive Visual Synthesis
summary: Recent advances in multimodal generative models have enabled instruction-based image generation to move beyond semantic manipulation to knowledge-driven visual reasoning. However, these methods focus on explicit commonsense reasoning, shallow causal understanding, and direct knowledge recall, failing at knowledge-intensive generation. We develop \textbf{ExpertVerse}, a capability-centric benchmark to evaluate generative models via knowledge-intensive lens. ExpertVerse stratifies reasoning generation across an orthogonal taxonomy of \textit{9 cognitive capabilities} and \textit{8 expert disciplines}, yielding \textit{58 sub-disciplines}. We curate 1,611 expert-annotated instances covering single-image editing, multi-image composition, and text-to-image generation. We further develop an automated workflow to produce \textbf{ExpertVerse-100K}, a large-scale dataset with reasoning traces and knowledge-anchored rationale annotations. Based on this, we train \textbf{KnowThinker} with RL fine-tuning, a VLM reasoning engine with world knowledge that jointly generates thinking processes and refined instructions. Towards the cross-modal credit misalignment and multi-objective gradient conflicts in multi-reward optimization, we propose a tailored Bootstrapped Pareto Policy Optimization (BPPO), which synergizes Bootstrapping Reward Rectification (BRR) and Conflict-Aware Pareto Advantage Fusion (CPAF). Extensive results of both open-source and proprietary models exposes critical reasoning deficits, highlighting imperative for knowledge-intensive benchmarks towards next-generation visual generation.

AI.tldr: Introduces ExpertVerse benchmark for knowledge-intensive multimodal generation evaluating 9 cognitive capabilities across 8 disciplines (58 sub-disciplines); 1,611 expert-annotated instances; ExpertVerse-100K dataset; KnowThinker model with RL fine-tuning; BPPO optimization to address cross-modal credit misalignment and gradient conflicts; shows gaps in current models and advocates knowledge-intensive benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Current multimodal generation methods focus on explicit commonsense reasoning or shallow knowledge recall, lacking robust capabilities for knowledge-intensive visual reasoning. A systematic, large-scale, knowledge-grounded benchmark is needed to evaluate and guide next-generation models.
AI.method: Design of a taxonomy with 9 cognitive capabilities x 8 expert disciplines (58 sub-disciplines); curation of 1,611 expert-annotated instances across single-image editing, multi-image composition, and text-to-image generation; automated workflow to produce ExpertVerse-100K with reasoning traces and knowledge-anchored rationales; training of KnowThinker (RL-finetuned VLM) to generate thinking processes and refined instructions; development of Bootstrapped Pareto Policy Optimization (BPPO) combining Bootstrapping Reward Rectification (BRR) and Conflict-Aware Pareto Advantage Fusion (CPAF) to manage multi-reward optimization.
AI.result: Extensive experiments across open-source and proprietary models reveal persistent reasoning deficits in knowledge-intensive tasks; the dataset and reasoning traces enable evaluation of knowledge-grounded generation; demonstrates imperative for knowledge-intensive benchmarks to drive progress in multimodal generation.
AI.conclusion: The work provides a comprehensive, knowledge-centric benchmark and accompanying methodology (KnowThinker with BPPO) to push multimodal models toward genuine knowledge-informed visual reasoning, highlighting gaps in current models and guiding future research.

title: Reinforcement Learning for Delivery Drone-Based Participatory Sensing in Dynamic Environments
summary: Using Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) for urban sensing has emerged as a powerful paradigm to monitor the status of the city, e.g., air quality and noise levels, through agile aerial crowdsourcing. Despite this potential, existing UAV-based sensing approaches overlook environmental disturbances like wind that drastically impact drone velocity and energy efficiency. Consequently, directly applying existing methods to this joint delivery and sensing paradigm in dynamic environments faces two severe challenges: (1) scalability bottlenecks as fleet sizes expand; and (2) multi-timescale decision heterogeneity between macro task dispatching and micro velocity control. To tackle these, we formalize the problem as SensUAV and propose a Two TimeScale Reinforcement Learning framework (TSRL). Specifically, TSRL separates decision-making into two cooperative layers. At the macro level, a task-embedding sensing dispatcher handles scalability by separately encoding distinct task features and sequentially evaluating UAV suitability before task selection. At the micro level, a wind-aware velocity controller learns fine-grained velocity scheduling to adapt to dynamic environmental variations. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that TSRL significantly outperforms baselines, achieving average system profit improvements of 20.1% in Hangzhou and 46.6% in Shanghai.

AI.tldr: A two-time-scale reinforcement learning framework (TSRL) for SensUAV that decouples macro task dispatch from micro wind-aware velocity control to improve scalability and energy efficiency in UAV-based urban sensing, achieving notable profit gains.
AI.motivation: UAV sensing is hindered by wind disturbances and scalability limits; joint delivery and sensing in dynamic environments requires multi-timescale decisions.
AI.method: Formalize as SensUAV; two cooperative layers: macro-level task-embedding sensing dispatcher encodes task features and evaluates UAV suitability for task selection; micro-level wind-aware velocity controller schedules velocity for dynamic environmental variation; uses real-world data; sequential task selection and evaluation of UAVs; experiments on Hangzhou and Shanghai datasets.
AI.result: Outperforms baselines with average system profit improvements of 20.1% in Hangzhou and 46.6% in Shanghai.
AI.conclusion: TSRL mitigates environmental disturbances and scalability issues, enabling effective joint delivery and sensing in urban UAV networks; demonstrates strong empirical gains in real-world datasets.

title: Physics-Informed Super-Resolution of Atmospheric Data
summary: In the context of global warming, extreme events have become more frequent and intense, making their trustworthy detection and forecasting more important than ever. Yet, atmospheric observations lack sufficient spatial resolution, motivating atmospheric data downscaling as a way to reconstruct high-resolution data from coarse observations. This task is now being formulated as a super-resolution (SR) problem with machine learning methods featuring high efficiency. Nevertheless, it remains unclear whether the super-resolved atmospheric data still satisfies fundamental physics governing the Earth system, raising concerns about their trustworthiness in climate-related applications. In this work, we address this challenge by constraining SR models to respect hydrostatic primitive equations that represent multivariate atmospheric physics. First, we propose a Physics-Informed Super-Resolution (PISR) method involving multi-scale physics-informed objectives based on primitive equations. PISR favors the SR outputs to respect these equations and therefore naturally encodes inter-variable relationships. In addition, we propose a metric called Normalized Physical Consistency (NPC) derived from said primitive equations to measure the physical consistency of super-resolved data. Experiments on ERA5, CERRA, and COSMO demonstrate that PISR enhances the reconstruction fidelity by improving physical consistency, SR accuracy, and downstream detection of extreme events, as demonstrated by case studies in heatwaves and extreme winds.

AI.tldr: Physics-informed super-resolution (PISR) for atmospheric downscaling enforces hydrostatic primitive equations and introduces NPC to ensure physical consistency, improving SR accuracy and extreme event detection on ERA5, CERRA, and COSMO data.
AI.motivation: Ignore the risk that standard SR can violate fundamental Earth-system physics when upscaling coarse atmospheric data; a physically grounded SR framework is needed to trust downstream climate analyses and extreme-event detection.
AI.method: Develop PISR: a multi-scale physics-informed SR framework constrained by hydrostatic primitive equations; integrate these PDE-based constraints into the SR loss to enforce inter-variable relationships; introduce Normalized Physical Consistency (NPC) as a metric derived from the primitive equations to quantify physical fidelity.
AI.result: PISR improves reconstruction fidelity, enforces physical consistency, enhances SR accuracy, and boosts downstream extreme-event detection in benchmarks (ERA5, CERRA, COSMO), with case studies on heatwaves and extreme winds.
AI.conclusion: Incorporating primitive-equation physics into SR training yields more trustworthy high-resolution atmospheric data and provides a quantitative physical-consistency metric (NPC), benefiting climate-related analyses and extreme-event studies.

title: Appearance Pointers -- Multimodal Region Control of Diffusion Transformers
summary: Controllable image generation remains challenging for creative professionals, who often require precise regional control over materials, object identities, and spatial arrangements that cannot be reliably achieved through text prompting alone. Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) can natively ingest heterogeneous tokens stemming from texts and images, but they lack mechanisms for determining where and how these tokens should influence the output. We introduce appearance pointers, compact tokens that guide DiTs toward the correct appearance cues at the correct spatial locations by aligning text or image inputs with user-specified masks. Appearance pointers are produced by a region correspondence network and refined through a spatial aggregation mechanism, enabling the model to handle multiple regional descriptions without significantly increasing token load. Our approach introduces the first modality-agnostic interface for localized multimodal control in a DiT without retraining the base model from scratch. Across a range of metrics, our single model reaches or surpasses the performance of modality-specific state of the art methods, offering a simple and extensible path toward precise, region-aware, multimodal guidance in generative image synthesis.

AI.tldr: Introduce appearance pointers for diffusion transformers to enable region-aware multimodal control without retraining. They are compact tokens produced by a region correspondence network and refined via spatial aggregation to align inputs with user masks, enabling multiple regional descriptions with low token overhead.
AI.motivation: Text prompts alone are insufficient for precise regional control in image generation; diffusion transformers lack localization mechanisms to determine how tokens influence output. A modality-agnostic, region-aware interface would enable precise control over appearance, region, and object identity across modalities.
AI.method: Propose appearance pointers, compact tokens that guide DiTs to correct appearance cues at specific spatial locations by aligning text or image inputs with user-provided masks. Pointers are produced by a region correspondence network and refined through a spatial aggregation mechanism, enabling multiple regional descriptions with minimal token load, without retraining the base model from scratch.
AI.result: A single model achieves or surpasses modality-specific SOTA across multiple metrics, matching or exceeding performance while providing a simple, extensible path toward precise region-aware multimodal guidance in generative image synthesis.
AI.conclusion: The work presents the first modality-agnostic interface for localized multimodal control in a diffusion transformer without retraining, enabling accurate region-aware guidance and broad applicability across modalities.

title: RAMP: Recognition parametrisation by Amortised Message Passing
comment: In the proceedings of the Symposium on Probabilistic Machine Learning 2026 (ProbML 2026)
summary: A central aim of unsupervised learning is to uncover latent factors that explain dependencies among observations. Probabilistic models typically achieve this by introducing multiple latent variables linked through a graph of conditional relationships, with distributional parameters and their dependence learnt from data. Learning relies either on distributional choices that allow tractable belief propagation, or on approximations that scale poorly with model size and complexity. We build on the recently developed recognition-parametrised modelling paradigm to propose an alternative approach: RAMP, a method that implicitly defines latent structure by learning a flexible, nonlinear, amortised message-passing framework. We show that RAMP enables efficient likelihood-based recovery of latent-variable distributions within expressive nonlinear models acting on complex high-dimensional data.

AI.tldr: RAMP introduces recognition-parametrised modelling to implicitly define latent structure via an amortised nonlinear message-passing framework, enabling efficient likelihood-based recovery of latent variables in complex nonlinear, high-dimensional data.
AI.motivation: Standard probabilistic models with multiple latent variables rely on tractable inference or costly approximations; there is a need for scalable, flexible latent-variable inference in high-dimensional data.
AI.method: Propose RAMP within the recognition-parametrised modelling paradigm; uses a flexible, nonlinear, amortised message-passing network to implicitly define latent structure rather than explicit graphical models.
AI.result: The approach enables efficient likelihood-based recovery of latent-variable distributions in expressive nonlinear models applied to high-dimensional data.
AI.conclusion: RAMP provides a scalable alternative to traditional belief-propagation or approximate inference, facilitating latent-variable recovery in complex models.

title: KALE: Kernel Alignment with Loss Equilibration for Stable CLIP-DINOv2 Alignment at Web Scale
summary: Kernel-based alignment of CLIP toward a vision centric teacher such as DINOv2 (KUEA) improves CLIP's visual representations while preserving text-encoder compatibility, using a fixed trade-off weight tuned on curated ImageNet-1K. We ask whether this transfers to noisy, web-scale data (CC12M) and find that it does not: the alignment term's weighted contribution falls to about 0.2% of the clean term, so under any fixed weight its gradient is effectively inert. We introduce KALE, a loss-equilibration controller that tracks both losses and adaptively rescales the alignment weight toward a target ratio, restoring the signal with no per-dataset tuning; reaching balance requires increasing the weight by roughly four orders of magnitude, and the required value is configuration-dependent, so no fixed scalar suffices. We characterize the resulting regime: a bounded high learning rate and a decaying schedule with a moderate floor are needed for stability, and the controller equilibrates rather than diverging. On a 3.3M-image CC12M subset, the aligned model preserves image-text retrieval and reproducibly improves SVHN linear probing; zero-shot improves by +2.00 over CLIP on the standard 11-dataset average, exceeding KUEA's +1.29. We report all results with explicit run-to-run variance and base our conclusions on the metrics that are stable across runs.

AI.tldr: KALE enables loss-equilibration for CLIP alignment with a vision-centric teacher; an adaptive loss-weighting controller preserves the alignment signal on noisy web-scale data, improving zero-shot and maintaining retrieval without per-dataset tuning, outperforming KUEA.
AI.motivation: Fixed-weight alignment tuned on clean ImageNet-1K fails to transfer to noisy, web-scale CC12M because the alignment term becomes nearly inert; an adaptable mechanism is needed to maintain alignment signal across datasets.
AI.method: Introduce KALE (loss-equilibration controller) that monitors both the alignment loss and the base loss and adaptively rescales the alignment weight to achieve a target loss ratio. Characterize stability: requires a high learning rate with a decaying schedule and a modest floor; equilibrates rather than diverging. Validate on a 3.3M-image CC12M subset, assessing image-text retrieval, SVHN linear probing, and zero-shot on 11 datasets; report run-to-run variance.
AI.result: On CC12M-3.3M subset, the aligned model preserves image-text retrieval and reproducibly improves SVHN linear probing; zero-shot improves by +2.00 on the 11-dataset average, beating KUEA (+1.29). A fixed weighting fails because the alignment term is negligible under noise; achieving balance requires increasing the weight by ~four orders of magnitude and is configuration-dependent.
AI.conclusion: KALE restores the alignment signal without per-dataset tuning, achieving stable equilibrated training that supports robust visual-language alignment on web-scale data, with results reported across multiple runs to demonstrate reproducibility.

title: Breaking Feedback-Blindness: Utility-Augmented Transformer for Sequential Decision Making
summary: Sequential decision making in non-stationary and partially observable environments requires rapid adaptation to latent regime changes. However, existing Transformer decision models face a structural bottleneck in the retrieval mechanism: even when reward is used for training or exposed as an input token, attention retrieval remains primarily driven by observation-derived similarity. We formalize this limitation as feedback-blind retrieval, and formally show that, on feedback-informative tasks, observation-equivalent histories with different action-reward outcomes cannot be distinguished by any observation-only attention, resulting in suboptimal choice. To address this mismatch, we propose the Utility-Augmented Transformer (UAT), a new feedback-conditioned retrieval attention architecture in which a compact utility state modulates the query, key, and value projections, allowing action-reward history to directly alter context retrieval during the forward pass. UAT also enjoys an exact zero-gate degradation property that recovers the Vanilla Transformer when feedback is uninformative.
